whatItIs: CEnT-S is the unified CISIA English admission test for many English-taught bachelor (and some single-cycle scientific) programmes in Italy. From November 2025 it replaces the old English TOLC types (English TOLC-I, English TOLC-E, English TOLC-F) for Engineering, Economics, Pharmacy, and other scientific fields taught mainly in English.
whoNeedsIt: Students applying to English-taught first-cycle degrees in Engineering, Economics / Business / Management, Pharmacy, Biotechnology / Biology, and many other science programmes where the university call requires CEnT-S. It is NOT the Medicine test — Medicine / Dentistry / Veterinary use IMAT. Politecnico di Torino engineering programmes use TIL-I instead of CEnT-S.

scoringNote: You see raw correct / incorrect / blank counts immediately. The final normalised score appears in the CISIA Student Area only at the end of the macro-period (by 30 Jan / 31 Mar / 30 Jun / 30 Oct depending on period). One attempt per macro-period; you may sit again in later periods.
howToUseScore: Book CEnT-S on the CISIA portal (you can sit at any participating venue, not only your target university). Apply separately on each university portal / call. Some universities use only selected sections (for example Mathematics + Reasoning). Always read the programme admission notice.
exceptions: Politecnico di Torino English engineering bachelor programmes → TIL-I (not CEnT-S)
Medicine / Dentistry / Veterinary English single-cycle → IMAT via Universitaly
Some humanities / law / psychology English tracks may use different selection rules — confirm the call
notes: English TOLC-I / TOLC-E / TOLC-F names on older pages are outdated for A.Y. 2026/27 — expect CEnT-S in new calls.
Fee is €55 per attempt (credit card or Italian MAV).
Score validity and which sections count are set by each university call — confirm deadlines before booking.
Pharmacy English at Bologna–Rimini and Tor Vergata typically use CEnT-S (or university selection based on it), not IMAT.
